Catalogue review · read on 6 October 2026

Google Skills for higher education leaders

All 1,330 items in the Google Skills catalogue, rated for what they offer a university building graduate and staff capability with AI. Use the priority lenses to start from a leadership question, or set the filters yourself.

Prepared by A/Prof Matt Sutton, CHE, Flinders University, with assistance from Claude (Anthropic), an AI model, for catalogue extraction, classification and drafting.

Read with caution. Only 81 of 1,330 items were reviewed in depth. The rest were classified by rule from their titles and descriptions, with AI assistance, and may contain mistakes. Ratings are one reviewer's judgement against a draft capability set. Check an item's own page before acting on any single entry.

Strong or Useful for any discipline
  • Mostly engineering training. Google Skills was formerly Google Cloud Skills Boost, and about three quarters of the catalogue trains cloud engineers, developers and data specialists.
  • A small useful core. The value for teaching sits in a few dozen short courses on generative AI concepts, judgement and responsible use, agents and health.
  • A badge shows participation. Badges and passed knowledge checks show that someone finished and recalled content. On their own they cannot evidence a learning outcome or support assurance of learning.
  • Access has conditions. Every learner needs a personal Google Account and a Google Developer Profile. Courses are free, while hands-on labs draw on 35 free monthly credits.
  • Tool fit varies. Many items teach Google products by name. The strongest items teach ideas that carry over to Microsoft 365 Copilot.

Human-Centered AI

StrongTransferable
Course15mIntroductoryFreeAny disciplineGeneral or business
Hybrid metacognitionDistributed cognitionEthical reasoning

Fifteen minutes is short enough to open a tutorial on when to hand a task over and when to keep it. Its language about human intuition is looser than the wording of the hybrid metacognition capability on regulation and escalation, so frame the discussion around what a student would do when they reach the edge of their competence.

Explore the vital transition from task-driven workflows to human-centric AI orchestration. You will learn to strategically distinguish between augmentation and automation, and how to balance machine efficiency with human intuition. Explore other content in the Gemini Enterprise Agent Ready (GEAR) program.

Module objectives (Google's text)
  • Keeping humans in the loop: Shift from manual task execution to human-centric AI orchestration. This module teaches you to balance machine efficiency with human intuition, ensuring a human-in-the-loop approach remains at the core of your generative AI strategy.

Critical Thinking in AI-Driven Workflows

StrongGoogle-framed
Course45mIntroductoryFreeAny disciplineGeneral or business
Critical thinkingEvaluative judgementHybrid metacognitionEthical reasoningDistributed cognition

The closest match to the idea of epistemic accountability, owning and defending AI-informed work, anywhere in the catalogue. Verification, accountability for the output and stress-testing are all inside one 45-minute course. The course claims you can confidently own a polished result, which is itself a good object for a judging-quality task. It is delivered in Gemini, but every move transfers to Copilot.

In a world where AI can generate ideas in seconds, true innovation now lies in the uniquely human ability to think critically. This course explores the dynamic intersection of human ingenuity and machine intelligence, shifting the human role from simply producing quick answers to exercising high-level judgment. Through hands-on interactivities and real-world simulations, you'll move beyond treating AI as a mere shortcut and learn to use it as a strategic thinking partner. You'll develop the skills necessary to handle the polished imperfection of AI outputs by refining, challenging, and verifying information to transform generic results into professional, high-impact assets that you can confidently own.

Module objectives (Google's text)
  • Critical thinking in AI-driven workflows: Transform generative AI from a basic shortcut into an active strategic partner by adopting a collaborative workflow built for everyone. In this core module, you'll establish what it means to be the human in the lead, shifting from using AI for quick answers to strategic decision-making that accelerates problem-solving. You'll explore how to use Gemini inside Google Workspace, transition from keyword searches to structured prompting using the role, task, and format framework, and navigate conversational feedback loops to refine, challenge, and verify outputs. Finally, you'll cover techniques for detecting bias and hallucinations, a seven-step workflow to stress-test ideas, and best practices for saving prompts and maintaining final accountability.

StrongGoogle-framed
Course1hIntroductoryFreeHealth-specificHealth
Digital literacyCritical thinking

The only health-specific course. Check it before recommending it widely, because the tools tour is Google Cloud developer products. It is a credible component for postgraduate study in digital health.

Specifically designed for healthcare professionals, this course demystifies generative AI, the latest breakthrough in artificial intelligence, and the large language models (LLMs) that drive it. Discover real-world applications of generative AI in healthcare settings and master the art of crafting effective prompts tailored to your goals. Explore other content in the Gemini Enterprise Agent Ready (GEAR) program.

Module objectives (Google's text)
  • Introduction: This module covers the course objectives and provides an overview of the course structure, which is an introduction to generative AI (Gen AI), and an introduction to large language models (LLMs).
  • Introduction to Generative AI for Healthcare: This module introduces generative AI, the most recent advancement in AI, and large language models (LLMs), the technology that powers it. It defines artificial intelligence, machine learning, supervised learning, unsupervised learning, and generative AI. It also explores different generative AI development tools on Google Cloud, such as Vertex AI Agent Builder, Vertex AI Studio, and Model Garden. Health domain use cases and data examples are used to demonstrate how Gen AI can be used for healthcare.
  • Large Language Models in Healthcare: This module describes how generative AI and large language models can be used for healthcare. It also describes medical foundation models, explains multimodal LLMs, and explores prompt design for specific healthcare examples.
  • Course Summary: Course Summary

Optimize Agent Behavior

StrongGoogle-framed
Course1hIntroductoryFreeTechnicalGeneral or business
Distributed cognitionDigital literacy

The most directly useful agent course for anyone building staff agents. The instruction-writing module maps onto problems met in building staff quiz and assessment agents. The code examples are Python, but the instruction patterns are not.

You’ve built your first agent—now it’s time to take it further. In this course, you’ll advance your skills by learning how to turn a basic AI agent into a sophisticated, precise assistant—applying advanced instructions, model selection, planning capabilities, and structured output patterns. Explore other content in the Gemini Enterprise Agent Ready (GEAR) program. Join the community forum for questions and discussions

Module objectives (Google's text)
  • Welcome: Welcome to the course.
  • Advanced instruction writing: This module transforms basic instructions into professional agent guidance systems. You’ll learn structured patterns for defining agent persona, role, boundaries, and communication style—turning simple prompts into sophisticated behavioral frameworks grounded in ADK best practices.
  • Structured output: This module transforms unpredictable text responses into reliable, structured JSON output that systems can parse and use. You’ll learn how to use Pydantic schemas to enforce output format, making your agents production-ready for integration with applications, databases, and workflows.
  • Choosing and configuring models: This module empowers you to strategically select models and configure generation parameters for optimal performance. You’ll learn when to use Flash versus Pro models, how to set safety thresholds, and how to fine-tune temperature and token limits—transforming basic agents into production-optimized systems.
  • Planning for complex tasks: This module adds multi-step reasoning to your agents, transforming them from reactive responders into thoughtful problem-solvers. You’ll learn how to enable Gemini’s built-in thinking capabilities using BuiltInPlanner, allowing agents to plan their approach before executing—essential for complex, multi-step tasks.
  • The journey you’ve taken: This module summarizes what you've accomplished in each module and revisits the real-world applications that you can build with your new skills. The module also provides a best practice checklist, a code patterns reference, common pitfalls to avoid, and other helpful reference resources.

StrongTransferable
Course1h 15mIntroductoryFreeTechnicalNon-profit

Drafting a personal use policy is a ready-made Year 1 activity for capability 3. Restricting a model to supplied files is a practical way into traceability for capability 5.

Building on the foundational workflows established in Daily Wins with AI for Nonprofits and the creative strategies from Optimize Creativity and Fundraising with AI, this course teaches you to automate complex administrative tasks using source-grounded AI. You will learn to transform unstructured data, such as meeting audio and siloed reports, into structured assets like project briefs and compliance checklists. Finally, you will apply the ACT Framework to draft a personal AI use policy, ensuring these AI experiences remain ethical and mission-aligned.

Agent Fundamentals

StrongTransferable
Course1h 30mIntroductoryFreeTechnicalGeneral or business
Digital literacyDistributed cognition

Vendor-neutral enough to sit under Copilot Studio work. A sound reading for staff who want to understand what they are building.

This course introduces the fundamentals of AI agents and explores where agents add value in the real world. It provides a foundation for developers, architects, and technical decision-makers who want to understand AI systems through the lens of autonomous, goal-directed behavior. Explore other content in the Gemini Enterprise Agent Ready (GEAR) program.

Module objectives (Google's text)
  • Welcome: This module welcomes learners to the course.
  • Introduction to AI agents: This module gives a conceptual overview of AI Agents. Discover how AI Agents use autonomous action and reasoning to solve complex problems. You’ll explore the technical architecture—models, tools, and orchestration—that enables agents to learn, plan, and achieve goals on your behalf.
  • Agent abstraction: This module introduces the fundamentals of AI agents and why they represent a paradigm shift away from simple LLMs. You’ll learn the difference between language models that can only discuss solutions to agents that can autonomously execute them.
  • How agents work: This module reveals the internal architecture that powers every AI agent. You’ll explore how three fundamental components—the model, tools, and orchestration—work together. This powerful combination transforms static language models into autonomous systems capable of continuous, goal-directed action.
  • Agents in action: This module equips you with a practical decision-making framework for determining when agents are the right solution. You'll learn to identify scenarios where agents provide exceptional value, recognize anti-patterns where simpler solutions might be better, and make informed architectural decisions for your specific use case.
  • Course wrap up: You've completed the foundational course on AI agents and now possess a clear understanding of what agents are, how they work, and when to use them. This theoretical foundation will serve as your north star as you progress to building real agent systems in upcoming courses.

Responsible AI: Applying AI Principles with Google Cloud

StrongGoogle-framed
Course2hIntroductoryFreeAny disciplineGeneral or business
Ethical reasoningCritical thinking

Best used as a case to critique rather than a framework to adopt. Students can test a vendor's own ethics framing against the Ahpra codes, which also builds ethical reasoning without compelled tool use, because no Google AI tool is needed.

As the use of enterprise Artificial Intelligence and Machine Learning continues to grow, so too does the importance of building it responsibly. A challenge for many is that talking about responsible AI can be easier than putting it into practice. If you’re interested in learning how to operationalize responsible AI in your organization, this course is for you. In this course, you will learn how Google Cloud does this today, together with best practices and lessons learned, to serve as a framework for you to build your own responsible AI approach.

Module objectives (Google's text)
  • Module 1: In this module, you will learn about the impact of AI technology and Google's approach to responsible AI, and also be introduced to Google's AI Principles.
  • Module 2: In this module, you will learn about how to make a business case for responsible AI, based on the report 'The Business Case for Ethics by Design' by the Economist Intelligence Unit.
  • Module 3: In this module, you will learn about ethical dilemmas and how emerging technology such as generative AI can surface ethical concerns that need to be addressed.
  • Module 4: In this module, you will learn about how Google’s AI Principles were developed and explore the ethical aims of each of these Principles.
  • Module 5: In this module, you will learn about the practical application of responsible AI and how to operationalize AI principles by setting up and running reviews.
  • Module 6: In this module, you will learn about the process of identifying possible ethical issues and identify issue spotting questions to think critically about the potential benefits and harms of a use case.
  • Module 7: In this module, you will learn about the next steps and resources you can use to continue your responsible AI journey.

Artificial Intelligence (AI) offers transformative possibilities, but it also introduces new security challenges. This course equips security and data protection leaders with strategies to securely manage AI within their organizations. Learn a framework for proactively identifying and mitigating AI-specific risks, protecting sensitive data, ensuring compliance, and building a resilient AI infrastructure. Pick use cases from four different industries to explore how these strategies apply in real-world scenarios.

Module objectives (Google's text)
  • The What and Why of AI Security: This module introduces you to the core concepts of AI security. You'll explore the reasons why securing AI systems is crucial in today's world, gain a basic understanding of how AI works, and learn about the various ways we interact with AI and how that impacts security.
  • Creating a Secure AI Framework: This module guides you through the creation of a robust framework to protect your AI initiatives. You'll explore how AI is transforming the security landscape, the key components of a strong security foundation, and the SAIF framework—a strategic approach to maintaining AI security. You'll learn the six core elements of SAIF and their real-world application through use cases across four different industries.
  • Conclusion: This concluding module reviews key concepts from the course, and provides additional resources to guide you on your continued AI security journey.

Add Agent Guardrails with Callbacks

UsefulGoogle-framed
Course1hIntermediateFreeTechnicalGeneral or business
Ethical reasoningDistributed cognition

Audit trails are traceability in engineering form, which gives a concrete analogy for capability 5.

You’ve built capable agents with powerful tools—now ensure they operate safely and reliably. Use callbacks as observation points and control mechanisms. Monitor what’s happening, validate inputs and outputs, implement guardrails, and gain confidence that your agents behave in production.

Module objectives (Google's text)
  • Understanding callbacks: Callbacks are the foundation for monitoring, controlling, and ensuring safe agent execution. This part introduces callback fundamentals that you’ll use throughout the rest of the lesson.
  • Agent callbacks for flow control: Agent callbacks operate at the highest level, wrapping the entire agent execution. This part teaches you to control complete agent behavior with session management and access control.
  • Model callbacks for safety: Model callbacks provide critical safety checkpoints around LLM interactions. This part teaches you to validate inputs before they reach the LLM and sanitize outputs before they reach users.
  • Tool callbacks for validation: Tool callbacks provide critical checkpoints around tool execution. This part teaches you to validate tool arguments, enforce authorization, and create audit trails before and after tools run.
  • Production callback patterns: This final part brings together everything you’ve learned to create production-ready agents. You’ll combine callback types, implement caching for performance, and apply best practices for deployment.

Digital literacy

Needs Python. The description and instruction distinction is the part that carries over to Copilot Studio.

Turn your understanding of agents into practical reality by building, configuring, and running your first AI agent using Google’s Agent Development Kit (ADK). In this hands-on course, you’ll set up a complete ADK development environment, create agents with both Python code and YAML configuration, and run them through multiple interfaces. You’ll also learn the core parameters that define agent behavior, taking what you learned in course 1 and applying it to working code.Explore other content in the Gemini Enterprise Agent Ready (GEAR) program

Module objectives (Google's text)
  • Welcome: Welcome to the course.
  • Environment setup: This module transforms theory into practice by setting up your complete development environment. You’ll install Python, configure the Agent Development Kit (ADK), obtain API credentials, and create your first agent project, laying the essential foundation needed to start building agents.
  • Understanding your first agent: This module decodes the anatomy of an agent via the four core parameters that define its identity and behavior. You’ll learn to distinguish between description (what other agents see) and instruction (how this agent acts) and to write instructions that shape agent personality and capabilities.
  • Other ways to run your agent: This module expands your agent execution toolkit beyond the web interface, introducing three distinct deployment methods: Terminal commands for quick testing, API servers for production deployments, and programmatic execution for integration into larger applications.
  • Agent configuration with YAML: This module introduces a code-free alternative to defining agents through YAML configuration files. You’ll learn when declarative YAML configurations provide advantages over Python code for agent definition and how to create and manage YAML-based agents.
  • The journey you’ve taken: In just 75 minutes, you’ve transformed from understanding agent concepts to actually building and running your own AI agents. You’ve set up a complete development environment, created agents from scratch, experimented with different execution modes, and learned both Python code and YAML configuration approaches. This is no small feat. You've taken the critical step from theory to practice.

Method. Every title in the catalogue was screened, and about 150 items with an AI, ethics, health or agent angle were read in full. 81 items were rated by hand against six capabilities: evaluative judgement, critical thinking, ethical reasoning, digital literacy, distributed cognition and hybrid metacognition. All other items received a subject group and a default rating by rule, and their capability fields are left blank on purpose. Discipline reach and sector setting were assigned by rule for every item. Descriptions and module objectives are Google's own text, since Google publishes no formal learning outcomes.
Attribution. Prepared by A/Prof Matt Sutton, CHE, Flinders University. Catalogue extraction, rule-based classification and drafting were done with assistance from Claude (Anthropic). All ratings and notes should be read as preliminary and may contain mistakes.
Source. Google Skills catalogue and item pages, read on 6 October 2026. The catalogue changes often.
